title: Forcible Removal — Arbitrary Detention, Collusion, and Cover‑Up by PDI and LATAM
category: Arbitrary Detention / Abuse of Authority / Obstruction of Justice

confidence.note: V10 validated. 2 established articles (Art. 19 N°7: 0.821, Art. 19 N°3: 0.714). 10 authority stubs (all unverified). 5 segments, 14 nexus entries. Art. 19 N°7 is the primary anchor with the highest single-article score. Three-phase structure (removal → collusion → cover-up) correctly captured.

allegation_summary: On 5 July 2024, PDI officers forcibly removed passenger [[SPK-passenger-leandro]] from LATAM flight LA8159 at Santiago Airport solely on the basis of an unverified accusation of aggression by a LATAM [[SPK-stewardess-accuser]]. After the removal, PDI/DGAC officials reviewed CCTV, confirmed no aggression had occurred, and then colluded with LATAM staff to fabricate a post‑hoc justification and conceal the exculpatory evidence. Throughout the following hours, LATAM's security chief and ground staff systematically denied the passenger information, provided a falsified generic report, and applied a false 'disruptive passenger' label that led to a boarding denial the next day. This constitutes arbitrary detention, abuse of public office, obstruction of justice, and a continuing violation of constitutional rights.
evidentiary_strength: Extensive transcript evidence across STG‑6, STG‑7, STG‑12, STG‑13, STG‑16, STG‑29, Terminal_T2, and Dartnell_2. The PDI officer's own admission of no aggression (STG‑7.seg‑55) is captured on audio; the coaching session is audible in STG‑7; LATAM's information blackout and false labelling are recorded. Carabinero statements corroborate that false aggression claims are a routine airline practice.
legal_theory: Arbitrary Detention (Art. 19 N°7) aggravated by post‑removal collusion and obstruction of justice (Art. 19 N°3 due process). The cover‑up and systemic denial of information also support claims under the Criminal Code (abuse of office, falsification) and the Civil Code (intentional tort).
